blocks.title: Wire your local magpie into Astravia, installed and started in one click
blocks.description: The panel reads the vendor's release feed, verifies the published SHA-256, installs into your user directory per platform, then starts the gateway as a plugin child process — PowerShell into %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, sh into ~/.local/bin on macOS and Linux. No terminal, no administrator rights.

showcase.user_prompt: Start my local magpie and use its models.
showcase.assistant_reply: Gateway up; 37 models published to Astravia.

items.title: Install and start, one button
items.description: The panel finds an execution surface itself: powershell on Windows, sh on macOS/Linux. When neither runs, it reports what it tried instead of claiming the platform is unsupported.

items.title: The digest decides
items.description: Download hosts are restricted to the vendor's, and bytes are verified against the feed's SHA-256 (Get-FileHash on Windows, shasum/sha256sum elsewhere). A mismatch never lands.

items.title: Follows the host theme
items.description: Every surface uses host theme tokens (card / border / muted / primary), so light, dark and theme packs need no code changes.

items.title: Models land in Astravia
items.description: One click publishes the gateway's current catalogue as a host provider; disconnecting removes only the entry this plugin wrote.

items.title: Read the state
items.description: Opening the panel probes /api/version and reads back whether a binary exists.

items.title: Install and start
items.description: Without a binary the button becomes Install and start; with one it runs serve on the same port the panel probes.

items.title: Publish models
items.description: Once the gateway answers, one click writes its catalogue into the host model registry.

blocks.content: The gateway is a child process of this plugin and stops with Astravia. For a boot-time daemon, run magpie daemon install once after installing.
